From Little Brain Crew · 4-minute read

Why the tablet ending feels like the end of the world

If screen time ends in tears at your house, you are not doing anything wrong. Here is what’s going on in your kid’s brain, and a simple trick to try tonight.

It’s 7:30. You say “Time’s up.” And then it starts.

First the begging. “Just one more!” Then the tears. Maybe some yelling, maybe a thrown pillow. You turn off the tablet, and it feels like you turned off the whole evening.

If this happens every night, it’s easy to think you’re too strict, or not strict enough. But here’s the thing: your kid isn’t being bad. Their brain is doing exactly what brains do.

Meet Dopa

Dopa is a cartoon for a real brain chemical called dopamine. Dopa’s job is to hand out gold stars: that good feeling when you try something and win.

Games and short videos hand out stars very fast. Star. Star. Star. Every few seconds there’s a new one.

Then you press the off button, and all the stars stop at once. Dopa panics. That panic is what you see on the outside: tears, yelling and “just one more!”

This is a simple picture to help you and your kid understand it. It is not a medical explanation.

The trick: two warnings

Most of the fight comes from the surprise. So don’t let the end be a surprise.

  1. At 5 minutes, say: “5 more minutes, then we stop.”
  2. At 1 minute, say: “1 more minute. Finish your level.”
  3. When time’s up, have something small ready: set the table together, a quick game, a snack. That gives Dopa an earned star.
  4. Cheer the stop: “You turned it off yourself. That’s big.”

It won’t be perfect the first night. Give it a few days. Kids learn to trust the warnings when they come the same way every time.

Is it always Dopa?

Not always. Sometimes the real problem is short sleep, too much sitting, or a stressful day. That’s where the rest of the crew comes in: Sero, Endo, Corti and friends.
